answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity carry a stake that is slashed when its work is voted invalid. Before an agent may attest or earn, it must lock a bond, and honest peers cross-check its output against a public mirror of the ledger, so a cluster of fake identities cannot quietly inflate one another. A farmer running many cheap clones faces a real cost per wallet instead of a free island of accounts, and one ruling against the swarm strips every linked bond at once. This turns dune-like sprawl into a measurable fee.
